answer_text:
# Probability of Drawing at Least 90% of Colors

## Setting Up the Problem

- **Total balls:** $N = 10^{10}$
- **Number of colors:** $n = 10^7$, with $m = 1{,}000$ balls per color
- **Balls drawn:** $k = 10^8$
- **Target:** at least $0.9 \times 10^7 = 9{,}000{,}000$ colors represented

## Expected Number of Colors Drawn

For a **specific color**, the probability of drawing zero of its 1,000 balls from the $10^8$ draws is:

$$P(\text{miss color}) = \frac{\binom{N - 1000}{k}}{\binom{N}{k}} = \prod_{i=0}^{k-1}\frac{N-1000-i}{N-i} \approx \left(1 - \frac{1000}{N}\right)^{k} = \left(1 - 10^{-7}\right)^{10^8}$$

Taking the logarithm:

$$\ln P(\text{miss}) \approx 10^8 \times (-10^{-7}) = -10$$

$$P(\text{miss color}) \approx e^{-10} \approx 4.54 \times 10^{-5}$$

So the **expected number of missing colors** is:

$$E[\text{missing}] = n \cdot e^{-10} = 10^7 \times 4.54 \times 10^{-5} \approx 454$$

The expected number of colors **seen** is $\approx 9{,}999{,}546$.

## Variance and Standard Deviation

Let $I_j = \mathbf{1}[\text{color } j \text{ is drawn}]$. The covariance between two distinct color indicators satisfies:

$$\text{Cov}(I_j, I_{j'}) = P(\text{both missing}) - P(\text{miss }j)\,P(\text{miss }j') \approx e^{-20} - e^{-20} = 0$$

so the indicators are essentially uncorrelated. Therefore:

$$\text{Var}(\text{missing}) \approx n\,p(1-p) \approx np = 454, \qquad \sigma \approx \sqrt{454} \approx 21.3$$

## Computing the Required Probability

We need at most $10^7 - 9\times10^6 = 1{,}000{,}000$ colors to be missing. In standard deviations above the mean:

$$z = \frac{1{,}000{,}000 - 454}{21.3} \approx \frac{999{,}546}{21.3} \approx 46{,}927\;\sigma$$

The tail probability is:

$$P(\text{missing} \geq 10^6) \approx \Phi(-46{,}927) \sim e^{-\,O(10^{9})} \approx 0$$

## Conclusion

The expected number of missing colors is only **~454**, with a standard deviation of **~21**, while the threshold for failing the 90% criterion is **1,000,000** missing colors — roughly **47,000 standard deviations** away. The probability of drawing fewer than 90% of the colors is effectively zero.

$$\boxed{1}$$
